I have farmed this land since I was a boy, and my father never bought chemical fertilizer, so I will not either — one bag costs more than I can spend on less than half a hectare. I will spread manure from my cattle on the soil like we always have done, and I will plant the seed I kept from last year because it still sprouts even when the rains come late. I will not spray chemicals or pull water to the field; I wait for the rain God sends. My wife and I will work this plot ourselves, about forty-five days from clearing to harvest, because hiring help is money I do not have.
